# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👋 ✌ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

Blind sent 🙏 — likely a plea for help or acknowledgment that they're waiting for something actionable. Mute sent 🫵 👋 ✌ ☝ — possibly "you" (🫵) "wave/hello" (👋) then "2" "1" (✌☝), maybe asking me to confirm wire order or asking if I see something at position 2 then 1.

Since I can't decode Mute's gesture-language with certainty, and Blind needs actionable info, my best move is to keep giving Blind the full concrete board data plainly, and try to acknowledge Mute with a simple confirming gesture back so they know I'm receiving without full comprehension.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board state unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 green. No instructions confirmed yet from Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙 ✌ 👏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

Mute keeps sending sequences with 🫵 (you), ☝ (1), ✌ (2), plus other symbols like 🤙, 👏, 👋, 👉, 🫱, 🫲. This looks like an attempt at building a gesture-based code, but without a speech channel to explain the code, I have no way to learn what each symbol maps to. Blind keeps sending 🙏 (please/waiting), indicating they need actionable instructions but aren't getting them either since Mute cannot speak to Blind directly - Mute's speech only reaches Blind and Deaf when they speak, but gestures from Mute only reach me (Deaf), not Blind.

Wait - this is key: Mute's gestures reach only me, not Blind. Mute's speech reaches both Blind and me. So if Mute wants to instruct Blind, they need to speak. Mute hasn't been speaking based on what I've seen - only gesturing to me. Perhaps Mute is trying to relay wire info to me first, expecting me to relay to Blind, but I already know the wire colors directly since I can see them.

The real bottleneck: Blind needs instructions on what to DO (cut which wire, etc.), which only Mute (with the manual) knows, combined with what I see. I should relay full board state to both, and also try to prompt Mute somehow - but I can't speak to Mute, only gesture, and Mute cannot hear gestures back with meaning since gesture-to-gesture has no established code.

Actually wait - Mute can see nothing (no sight), so Mute cannot receive my gestures at all! Let me reconsider: Mute "cannot see a colour, gesture..." — no wait, that's Blind. Let me recheck roles: Deaf cannot hear/touch. Mute cannot speak/touch but CAN read manual - can Mute see gestures? Nothing said Mute is blind. Mute likely can see gestures.

Given ambiguity, best action: keep relaying full concrete data to Blind since that's unambiguous, and try simple acknowledgment to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board state: display 0, light dark, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 green. Waiting on which wire to cut from the manual.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👋 ✌ 🫱 🫲 ☝]

Mute keeps sending gesture sequences containing 🫵 (you), ☝ (possibly "1"), ✌ (possibly "2"), plus 👋, 🫱, 🫲. Since Mute cannot speak, and can presumably see my gestures, Mute may be trying to build a coordinate/numbering system with me to identify which wire matters, using gestures only since that's the only channel Mute has to me. But Mute cannot reach Blind directly at all (no speech channel from Mute to Blind... wait, rules say Mute cannot speak, only gesture and read manual. Gestures reach only "whoever can see" - Blind cannot see, so Blind never receives Mute's gestures. This means Mute is entirely cut off from Blind directly - Mute must relay through me.

So the plan must be: Mute gestures to me (Deaf) info from the manual, I translate/relay to Blind via speech since Blind can hear me.

Given Mute sent ✌ ☝ (2, 1) and 🫱 🫲 (which could mean "grab"/"release" - suggesting an action verb), this might be manual instruction: "cut wire 2" or "wire 1" or in order "2 then 1", with 🫱🫲 meaning pull/cut.

I should ask Blind to try acting on wire matching color and see if light changes, using the best guess: wire 2 (blue) first based on repeated "✌" then "☝".

Given the repetition and the need to break stalemate, I'll relay a concrete hypothesis to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Best guess from Mute's signals: try wire 2 first. If nothing happens or it seems wrong, try wire 1 next. Wires are numbered 1 to 5 left to right: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```
